title: Connie's Inn: nightclub shows, wealthy downtown crowd, good pay
summary: Henderson's band at Connie's Inn doubled with the Lafayette, drew downtown stars like Clara Bow, and paid $90-100 a week during the Depression.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. The Big Trade, yeah. So then we went to work for Fletcher, down at Connie's Inn, which was -- for me it was a great move because I almost doubled my salary, you know, because oh, it was great. It was great. And it was my first time to sit in a band that was playing dance music and shows, nightclub shows, and at that time Connie's Inn was one of the top nightclubs.
This was when it was still next to the --

Right. Right. Right. Right. And very good. Plus we used to double. We used to call it double. You played like -- we'd play theaters. We'd play the Lafayette, we'd double at the Lafayette and then come downstairs. See, and the hours were so great. I think 10:00 to 3:00. 10:00 o'clock at night till 3:00 in the morning.
Did people come from the Lafayette, the customers, and go to Connie's afterwards?
Well, I suppose some people did. I

suppose some people did, but there was such a difference in the money, the prices. You could go to the Lafayette, I suppose, for -- oh, I don't know, I don't remember exactly what it cost to go to the show.
I think it was like a quarter at some time, or .50¢.

Well, I suppose something like that, but Connie's Inn was a different bracket entirely, you know. Most of the people who came to Connie's Inn came from downtown, you know. I remember seeing Clara Bow and Harry Richman. They were big stars, and nightclub stars and movie stars, and they came up their in an aluminum-bodied Rolls Royce. And this was the Depression, Depression for some people. Well, no Depression for the --

No, not for the movie people, not at all. And as such, I mean the Depression didn't -- you know, like I say, affect everybody, because there were some bands that just kept rolling, like Fletcher Henderson. In those days, you know, we made 90.00, $100.00 a week in Connie's Inn, which was pretty good money in those days.
